issues.description: The script establishes a WebSocket connection to garticphone.com and sends game drawing data packets, including user actions and possibly game state.
issues.recommendation: Ensure only necessary game data is transmitted; avoid sending sensitive or unrelated user information.

issues.description: The script modifies Node.prototype.appendChild to intercept and rewrite scripts loaded from external sources, potentially allowing remote code execution if the editScript function is abused.
issues.recommendation: Restrict script rewriting to trusted sources and validate edited code before execution.

issues.description: The script uses unsafeWindow to override WebSocket globally, which may introduce compatibility and security risks.
issues.recommendation: Limit unsafeWindow usage and ensure no leakage of sensitive data or unintended side effects.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission but does not use it in the code, indicating potential permission overreach.
issues.recommendation: Remove unused permissions to minimize attack surface.

issues.description: The script requests GM_log permission but does not use it in the code, indicating potential permission overreach.
issues.recommendation: Remove unused permissions to minimize attack surface.

issues.description: The script uses fetch to load external resources, but only from the same domain (garticphone.com). No third-party data exfiltration detected.
issues.recommendation: Monitor for future changes that may introduce third-party requests.

summary: The script transmits drawing/game data via WebSocket to garticphone.com, intercepts and rewrites loaded scripts (potential remote code execution risk), and requests unused permissions. No evidence of privacy collection or code obfuscation. The main risks are data transmission (CRITICAL) and remote code execution (HIGH).
